title: C3465 — Passenger upper side airbag connector reference
introduction:
I read this airbag reference like an address book: the drawing locates a labeled cavity, and the matching table row identifies its circuit. Start with the connector metadata, compare the illustrated housing features, then read across the cavity’s row. The pigtail table provides separate service-part references.

Keep the component naming question visible: the title describes an upper side airbag, while the circuit functions describe a seat-mounted passenger side airbag. That wording needs review before identifying the actual component.

This page explains the reference rather than teaching electrical testing or replacement. Physical viewing direction, access, release movements, test conditions and repair instructions are outside its scope. Gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes are unexplained; retain them as printed.

items.name: Qualified personnel and restraint-specific instructions
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Use the matching depowering, handling, test-equipment and restoration instructions. Do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test. Consult the [Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693191) and [SRS overview](#/document/G1696290); this connector reference does not supply those service sequences.

edits.why: I use the circular housing outline and vertically stacked cavity labels to navigate the printed drawing. The surrounding projections are visual landmarks; the illustration does not identify their release or locking functions. Read the labels in the drawing’s displayed orientation without assuming which side of a physical connector faces you.

Match a drawing label to the Cavity column, then read across that same row for circuit identity, color, gauge and function. Preserve the positive and negative function markings: they distinguish the listed circuit roles without supplying a test method. A terminal entry marked unavailable supplies no terminal selection.

Read each service-part entry together with its kit number and engineering shell. A shared shell entry does not explain how to choose between the listed pigtails. The image filenames identify referenced images rather than additional illustrations displayed here; this table supplies neither an installation sequence nor a replacement decision.

originalAuthorHold: Component identity needs review: the title says PASSENGER UPPER SIDE AIRBAG, while the circuit functions describe AIR BAG SIDE SEAT MOUNTED FRONT PASSENGER SIDE. The supplied evidence does not reconcile those descriptions.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 30 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Upper-side versus seat-mounted passenger airbag identity ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
